questions.question: Explain why a fridge with a power rating of 150 W can use more energy in a day than a 2 000 W kettle.
questions.expected_answer: Energy = power × time. The fridge runs for about 10 hours a day: 0,15 kW × 10 h = 1,5 kWh. The kettle is used for only about half an hour: 2 kW × 0,5 h = 1 kWh. The long running time makes the fridge's total energy larger despite its lower power.

questions.question: Describe how a flat-plate solar water heater works and why it should face north in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: A black plate and pipes under a glass cover absorb radiant energy from the Sun; the glass traps heat; the heated water rises into an insulated storage tank (thermosiphon) while cooler water sinks to the collector; a backup element heats water on cloudy days. In the Southern Hemisphere the Sun is in the northern part of the sky, so a north-facing collector receives the most sunlight.

questions.question: A geyser uses 270 kWh a month. A solar water heater would save 70% of this. Calculate the monthly saving at R2,50 per kWh and the payback time if the system costs R15 000.
questions.expected_answer: Saving = 0,7 × 270 = 189 kWh; 189 × R2,50 = R472,50 per month; payback = 15 000 ÷ 472,50 ≈ 31,7, so about 32 months (under three years).
